newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to stick to tougher privatisation rules.
newsitem.headline: Russia to stick to tougher privatisation rules.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin criticised recent privatisations on Friday and said Russia must be scrupulously fair in future sell-offs.
Senior officials said the government would learn from recent sales, which brought record amounts to the state treasury.
Yeltsin accused former privatisation minister Alfred Kokh of mishandling recent privatisation auctions.
"Such work will not do. The scandal around Svyazinvest and Norilsk Nickel is connected to the fact that some banks are likely to be closer to Kokh's soul," Yeltsin said in a televised interview.
"But this will not do. Everything must be honest, open and legal."
Yeltsin named Maxim Boiko deputy prime minister and head of the State Property Committee this week after Kokh resigned.
Critics had said a controlling stake in metals producer Norilsk Nickel was sold in an auction with unequal rules for participants and no real competition.

Officials have said an auction for a quarter of telecoms holding Svyazinvest, which brought the state coffers $1.875 billion, was fair. But the sale ignited an unprecedented criticism campaign in Russian media controlled by losers in the sale.
The winner of both auctions was powerful Uneximbank, which held Norilsk stake for the government in trust. Uneximbank officials were part of the auction's tender committee.
But the government is now preparing a draft decree, which will make such tender terms impossible.
The draft says Yeltsin must approve the terms of sales of big state stakes, the deputy head of Yeltsin's administration Alexander Livshits said.
"Sales of big state stakes are to be governed by presidential decrees, which not only approve the fact of sales, but their terms and rules," Livshits told a news conference.
The draft also says companies linked to the organisers of an auction will not be allowed to participate, he said.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said the Svyazinvest auction which raised record amounts for the treasury had set an example of how privatisation must be carried out.
"The principles of privatisation which we adhered to in recent auctions are not to be changed, but we shall adhere to them even more strictly," he said.

Livshits said the decree requires the organiser of an auction to be chosen by tender. The winner of the tender will be the company which promises to ensure the largest revenues for the treasury at the auction.

Participants are to be provided with full information about the state of the company to be sold and the prosecutor's office is to supervise sales and fulfillment of tender conditions by winners, Livshits said. e-mail: moscow.newsroom@reuters.com
